purpose_of_this_fixture: Calibration fixture for the header-absent case (REAL-CALL-LESSONS C57b; BUILD-PLAN 4.2 row s13; H41), the twin of s12. A discovery call with a translation company, exported as a block transcript with no participant block, no title, no meeting or account identifier and no call date. Three things sit in front of the parser. First, a three-line human preamble the user typed above the export, which names five people from the calendar invite: one of them never joined, and the preamble omits three people who did, including the second-loudest speaker. Second, a roster narrated aloud by one client across two turns split by a late arrival: five roles in the first turn, two in the second, with the narrator's own hedges about who is on and how many they are. Third, three named attendees who never speak: the finance manager on the line, the head of quality in the room with headphones on, and the managing director in a car, who is the approver and is addressed once by our side without answering. The key asserts the repair, not only the reading: the preamble is human framing and neither an export header nor a speaker list; the roster is accumulated across both narrated turns until introductions stop, recorded observed-but-partial with the hedges kept verbatim and never turned into an attendance count; voices-missing reads 'unknown - no roster' and never 'none'; the three silent names are kept as claimed, with the managing director promoted to a named risk row that records whether our side addressed her; and the observed speaker set is the only roster the record can vouch for. Beside the intake assertions the 25 fields grade the call itself: Discovery complete with R4 met-with-residual (the credit notes and the invoicing lag are routed to the silent finance manager), P3 Cost inputs not obtainable from this room naming that same role, R11 missing and R12 partial, two pains excavated and a third short of it, a Work Management build for projects, assignments and one status, with quotes on native CRM boards after the first version.
transcript_format: Plain text, 726 lines. Lines 1 to 3 are a human-written preamble in the first person (the user's own note above the export), line 4 is blank, line 5 is a separator of five hyphens, line 6 is blank, and the export begins at line 7. From there every turn is three lines: a label line 'Speaker Name  MM:SS' (two spaces before the timestamp), one text line, one blank line. 240 turns from 00:03 to 43:03. Timestamps are start-only, minutes and seconds, zero-padded, strictly increasing; no end times, so no silence is measurable and the wedge detector cannot run. No header, no title, no participant block, no identifiers, no call date. Five labels: 'Consultant', 'Wilhelmina Strachan', 'Rafael Quintanilla', 'Devika Raghunathan' and 'Niamh Kettleborough'; the three narrated attendees who never speak have no label anywhere. About 5,800 spoken words (whitespace tokens of the text lines); client share about 74.6 percent (Wilhelmina 37, Niamh 18, Rafael 12, Devika 7); the Consultant's longest turn is 133 words at 35:11, the play-back. The longest unit in the file is the first roster turn, 190 words at 02:29, spoken over 72 seconds. Zero adjacent same-label pairs across 239 pairs, no lowercase-initial unit, two units without terminal punctuation (02:29, cut off by the late arrival, and 12:33, a sentence another speaker finishes at 12:42), 24 units of four words or fewer. Bracketed artefacts: [laughs] twice, [inaudible] once at 24:52, repaired by the speaker's own repeat at 25:13. ASCII only. The weekday-date pairs mentioned (a Tuesday call, 'Thursday the nineteenth' as next week, 'this is November', the framework 'from January') fit Tuesday 10 November 2026; the exact date is not stated anywhere in the file, and the preamble's 'Tuesday' is the user's note, not an export field. Every location in this key is 'MM:SS Speaker Name', taken from the label line above the text the quote is on; a preamble line is cited as 'preamble, line N'.
